header.running_head: The Abstinence of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

blocks.text: The Abstinence of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)
The Narration of Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) narrates, "We were once with Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) when he asked for something to drink. When some water mixed with honey was brought and put in his hand, he started to cry and sobbed a lot. He wept so much that we thought that something was seriously wrong with him. However, we did not ask him anything. When he stopped crying, we asked, 'O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! What made you weep so much?' He replied, 'I was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I saw him repel something from himself which I could not see. I asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! What was it I saw you repel from yourself when I could see nothing?' He replied, 'The world leapt towards me and I (repelled it as I) said, 'Get away from me!' It then said, 'I know that you will never take me.' It was this that made it difficult for me (to drink the honey water). I feared that I may oppose the way of Rasulullaah ﷺ and that the world would get hold of me."[^1]

In another narration, Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once asked for a drink, he was given a cup with honey mixed in water. As he took it to his mouth, he started weeping and this made everyone around him cry as well. When he stopped crying, the people around him were still in tears. The same thing happened a second time and this time he cried so much that the people could not even ask him anything. When he eventually wiped his face and stopped crying, the people asked him the reason for his crying. The rest of the narration is similar to the one above except that he also said, "It (the world) then said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), 'Remember! I swear by Allaah that although you have slipped through my grasp, those after you will be unable to do so."[^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) Stating that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left Nothing Behind
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Abu Bakr (RA) passed away without leaving behind a Dinaar or a Dirham. Just before his demise, he took all his money and deposited it in the Baytul Maal."

Another narration from Hadhrat Urwa (RA) states that when he was made Khalifah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) deposited every Dinaar and Dirham he possessed into the Baytul Maal. He said, "I used to trade and seek my livelihood with this money. Now that I am the Khalifah, public affairs have preoccupied me from trade and earning a livelihood."[^3]

Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.254) has commented on the chain of narrators but Ibnul Mundhir (Targheeb wat Tarheeb Vol.5 Pg.168) says that the chain is sound and that Ibn Abi Dunya has also reported the narration.
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.30). Haakim and Bayhaqi have also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.37).
Ahmad in his Zuhd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.132).
